functionalObligations.text: a depositor exchanges the stablecoin for a share token whose nominal balance never changes and whose redemption value rises
interest compounds per second into a stored rate accumulator, advanced by a permissionless call and extrapolated exactly in view functions without writing state
functionalObligations.note: Sr is approximate: this is per-second compounding of an accumulator (chi = _rpow(ssr, now - rho) * chi / RAY), not the streaming of a claim to a named recipient. Live 2026-08-04: chi = 1.105245252046483725540827799, totalAssets = 4,750,051,555.68 USDS.

functionalObligations.text: the interest owed is funded by minting internal protocol debt against the system's surplus/deficit account, unconditionally, with no read of revenue, reserves or any solvency condition
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the mechanism is now named precisely: vat.suck(vow, this, diff*RAY) then usdsJoin.exit. Not Em (no separate token, no schedule); not Sl (no loss event — the deficit is created by the payment); not As (no peg rule drives it); not Fd (Fd is surplus distribution and this can run in deficit). The corpus's residue item 'a rate that can exceed protocol revenue' is confirmed. Restate the corpus's yield-source claim as funded ex post from the surplus buffer, not ex ante from realised revenue.

functionalObligations.text: the rate paid is a written number, not derived from a utilisation curve, an auction or any market; the only bound inside the savings token is that it be non-negative
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE. file('ssr') requires only data >= RAY. 'set by a vote' versus 'set by utilisation' versus 'set by a curve' are three different risk objects that decompose identically in this vocabulary. Confirmed at code level; the same administered-rate object appears independently at Huma 2.0 (8% APY, monthly adjustment).

functionalObligations.text: the rate may be written only by addresses enumerated in an on-chain set which governance may add to or remove from at any time
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent) and SLOT 5 (revocation), partial fit. Aw names the caller enumeration (buds[msg.sender] == 1) and its mutability. It does not name that what is being granted is a discretionary economic authority rather than a right to participate. Independently verified: sUSDS.wards(0x36B072ed8AFE665E3Aa6DaBa79Decbec63752b22) = 1. DEPARTURE: the corpus does not carry Aw for Spark.

functionalObligations.text: the enumerated agent chooses the value of the live savings rate at its own discretion, with no objective function, trigger, target or derivation anywhere in the code
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE — the headline of this lane, in its rate-setting form. Tg is wrong (the change is immediate). Au is wrong (L17 wants bounded scope + revocation + expiry + nonce/domain separation, i.e. a session key over the principal's own assets; a facilitator has no expiry, no nonce, and acts over the whole system's economics). Gp names the halt but not the authority it halts. The corpus's phrase 'set by a governance vote' is superseded: governance writes the bounds, a whitelisted facilitator writes the number inside them.

functionalObligations.text: the agent may write only parameters drawn from an enumerated set of rate identifiers, each with its own configuration record
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Live ids include 'SSR', 'DSR' and per-ilk stability fees. No symbol names a restriction of a delegated decision to a domain.

functionalObligations.text: the value written must lie between a governance-set floor and ceiling, live two per cent and thirty per cent
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call cfgs('SSR') = {min 200, max 3000, step 400} on 0x36B072ed8AFE665E3Aa6DaBa79Decbec63752b22, accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 3 (magnitude cap). RESIDUE. A numeric domain restriction on a delegated decision has no symbol; Ct is a solvency test, not a parameter envelope.

functionalObligations.text: a single update may move the rate by at most a governance-set step, live four percentage points, and no update may occur within a cooldown of the previous one, live sixteen hours; the update then takes effect immediately
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 4 (rate-of-change limit). RESIDUE. Note precisely what tau is: a cooldown SINCE the last change, not a delay BEFORE execution. Tg is therefore the wrong symbol twice over — the agent's change is immediate and does not pass the 48-hour governance pause that gates governance's own actions. Ep is wrong: there are no periods.

functionalObligations.text: the rate-setting module can be halted outright by an emergency contract, after which no agent may write anything
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (halt). Gp names the kill switch (bad != 0) but not the mandate it kills. A sibling module in the same ecosystem (pau-administered-agent) deliberately separates grantors from revokers so that revokers act as live watchdogs; Tg, Gp and Au all treat authority as a single scalar and cannot express that split.

functionalObligations.text: governance's own parameter changes execute only after a forty-eight-hour delay
a holder may redeem the share for the underlying stablecoin at the current accumulator value at any time
functionalObligations.note: Large mainnet withdrawals are routed through an off-chain 'Savings Liquidity Intents' request fulfilled within minutes; that routing is a service level, not a contract term, and is not decomposed.

functionalObligations.text: the underlying stablecoin swaps one-for-one against a reserve asset through a peg module at zero fee, subject to a buffer, with the fee range bounded in code
functionalObligations.evidence: https://ethereum-rpc.publicnode.com (eth_call tin() = 0, tout() = 0, buf() = 800,000,000 on 0xf6e72Db5454dd049d0788e411b06CfAF16853042, accessed 2026-08-04)
functionalObligations.note: INHERITED, corpus marker retained. The peg module belongs to the Sky/USDS system that the savings product sits on, not to the savings product. It is load-bearing for solvency while being invisible as a property of the thing decomposed; the vocabulary has no way to mark an element as inherited from a dependency.

functionalObligations.text: the savings claim is represented on six other chains by a token minted and burned against the mainnet position

the rate tuple (rate, accumulator, timestamp) is forwarded to each remote chain over that chain's canonical bridge and accepted only after application-level sanity checks including an upper bound on the rate and enforcement of event ordering
functionalObligations.note: DEPARTURE: the corpus carries neither Xm nor Ex for Spark. Xm names the canonical-bridge verification; Ex names the remote oracle that publishes the tuple. The maxSSR bound exists explicitly to bound the damage of a compromised bridge, which is L13-shaped freshness/validity validation.

functionalObligations.text: the remote token contains no accrual state and no drip function at all; its value is extrapolated locally from the forwarded tuple and its redeemability is limited by local peg-module inventory rather than by the mainnet balance sheet
functionalObligations.note: RESIDUE, and the corpus's version of this item is materially wrong rather than merely incomplete. The corpus assumed cross-chain sameness was economic identity; it is not. The mainnet claim can mint against the system's deficit account, the remote claim cannot. The unnamed object is a replicated index with a locally-bounded settlement guarantee. A construction that models the eight chains as one claim gets the failure modes wrong.

functionalObligations.text: the system's own capital — not the depositor's claim — is deployed into external protocols by a named multisig role, with custody of all deployed funds sitting in a single proxy
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 1 (named agent), partial fit, second instance at this application. SCOPE: obligations F17-F20 belong to the Spark Liquidity Layer, which DefiLlama files as a separate protocol in a separate category (Onchain Capital Allocator, $1.58bn). They are included because the newer Spark Savings vaults are documented as generating yield 'via the Spark Liquidity Layer', and because the same organisation shipping the claim and the mandate as different objects with different addresses is itself the evidence for a missing level. Verified: MainnetController.hasRole(RELAYER, 0x8a25A24EDE9482C4Fc0738F99611BE58F1c839AB) = 1.

functionalObligations.text: that role may act only through an enumerated set of twenty-nine venue-specific actions — mint, swap, deposit into a named vault, subscribe to a named fund, bridge by a named route — and cannot construct a new one
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 2 (domain whitelist). RESIDUE. Governance determines the use cases supported; the numeric value of each limit is UNKNOWN (the docs defer to Sky Atlas and per-key live values were not read).

functionalObligations.text: each enumerated action carries a maximum amount and a slope that regenerates spent capacity continuously with elapsed time
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOTS 3 and 4 fused (magnitude cap plus rate-of-change limit) into one leaky bucket: _min(slope * (now - lastUpdated) + lastAmount, maxAmount). RESIDUE. Not Ep (no discrete periods), not Wq (no ordering, no queue), not Ct (no solvency test). A continuously regenerating throughput allowance on an agent has no symbol, and it is the closest thing in the lane to a general form of the mandate envelope.

functionalObligations.text: a separate multisig can freeze the controller without being able to use it
functionalObligations.note: MANDATE SLOT 5 (halt). Gp names the freeze. It does not name that the right to halt is deliberately held by a different party from the right to act, which is the whole accountability design.

functionalObligations.text: the savings token itself sits behind an upgradeable proxy whose administrator is the governance pause proxy
functionalObligations.note: L15 is satisfied here: the upgrade path runs through the 48-hour pause proxy (F11). Not an obligation but a measurement hazard for stage 6: live sUSDS.totalAssets() = $4.750bn against DefiLlama's Spark Savings line of $1,132,142,962.30, so a paper figure must state which of the two it means.
